comparator.name: International Bachelor Econometrics and Operations Research
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 official study schedule and major table establish this 180-EC curriculum: Bachelor-1 60, Bachelor-2 60 and Bachelor-3 60 EC. The public prospective-student overview now labels its indicative curriculum 2027–2028; it is used only for general orientation, not current component/credit evidence. Econometrics is the broad continuation of the common field and first major in the current formal table. Its selected pathway comprises Advanced Econometrics (4), Quantitative Methods for Data Science (4; first listed eligible choice), and Seminar in Forecasting (12; first listed seminar). The minor12/electives12 branch is retained; the alternative minor15/electives9 branch is also permitted. The two distinct 1-EC Career Skills units are kept separate. Zero-credit Take-Off Bachelor and Guidance remain compulsory non-credit obligations; they are not added to 180 EC. TER articles10–12 and31 establish choices, attendance, BSA and progression. The English full-time BSc is the exact normalized target, not the Dutch programme or a double degree.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: Operations research, optimisation and decision models
Research practice, academic skills and ethics
adjacent: Analytics and Operations Research in Logistics
questions: How can real economic and business problems be translated into mathematical models and optimised?
How can data be used to estimate, forecast and support decisions under uncertainty?

trace: Specific complementary study of accounting information and financial statements helps interpret company data and economic events. The enriched content does not establish a full corporate-finance or quantitative-finance syllabus.

Specific complementary non-technical study of AI’s effects on business, labour markets, growth, governance and economic decisions supplies a defined application strand. It is not technical data-science training.

Direct practical work with financial data, risk, investment, budgeting and business decisions supplies the financial-decision strand. It does not establish specialist econometric asset-pricing or banking-model training.
provides the introductory microeconomic and macroeconomic framework needed for quantitative economic applications
develops macroeconomic analysis of growth, inflation, policy, crises and international trade using economic data
develops advanced microeconomic analysis of uncertainty, strategic behaviour, market structure, equilibrium and efficiency
uses theoretical models and empirical evidence to analyse market failure, taxation, redistribution and public policy
directly develops econometric estimation, testing, causal analysis, prediction and Monte Carlo simulation in Stata
develops evidence-based analysis of economic decision-making, biases and behavioural choice

Specific complementary venture study develops business-model and customer validation, market testing and business planning: concrete operating decisions underlying the business/financial strand. It also satisfies the formal prerequisite for Money, Banking & Finance; it is not counted as financial mathematics.
provides foundational research design, statistics and empirical-analysis skills for later econometric work
adds explicit ethical analysis of algorithmic systems, including fairness, accountability, privacy and responsibility
develops computational decision models under uncertainty, partial observability, constraints and resource limits
provides discrete mathematics, logic and algorithmic structures useful for formal decision and optimisation problems
develops search, constraint satisfaction and optimisation methods in discrete and continuous environments
develops algorithmic learning and sequential decision-making through reinforcement-learning models
deepens programming and software-development practice in multiple languages for computational data work
develops algorithm design, data structures and performance analysis for computational modelling
develops advanced algorithms and computational solution methods for optimisation problems
develops foundational data cleaning, visualisation and analysis through applied research projects
develops predictive modelling through regression, classification, resampling, tree methods and clustering

Direct neural-network theory and Python/TensorFlow implementation, including tabular data, computer vision and text applications, extends the computational data-science route. These broader applications are not represented as additional econometrics training.
provides the programming foundation in Python, computational problem-solving and basic discrete mathematics

Direct foundation in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations for mathematical modelling. Linear algebra is supplied separately by DISMATH211; the gateway outline is not credited with an eigenvalue syllabus.
develops matrix methods, vector spaces, linear transformations and systems of linear equations

Direct numerical treatment of equations, interpolation, differentiation, integration and ordinary differential equations, including accuracy and sensitivity. Its introductory mention of optimisation does not establish a specialist optimisation syllabus.
extends calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations for quantitative modelling

Specific complementary data infrastructure: relational models, normalization, SQL and query processing support collection and preparation of economic/business datasets. This is not econometric inference.
develops probability theory, distributions, sampling, estimation and simulation as a mathematical-statistics foundation

Specific complementary ethical theories and argumentation, including poverty, wealth, equality and responsibility, support evaluation of economic decisions. The course is not a substitute for profession-specific econometric ethics.
provides multivariate statistics, regression, factor analysis and related inference methods useful for complex empirical data

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics, econometrics & optimisation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around economics, econometrics and optimisation, supported by mathematics, statistics, programming, algorithms and data analysis; the label avoids presenting UCR as offering the comparator's full specialist econometrics sequence.
alternatives.concept: Mathematics, statistical inference and econometrics are combined with economics, programming, algorithms and computational optimisation to study quantitative economic and business problems.
progression: Programming and introductory economics begin in Semester 1, followed by calculus and research/statistics foundations. Linear algebra, probability, machine learning and Algorithms & Data Structures precede advanced algorithms and optimisation. Multivariate statistics precedes Econometrics. Advanced Calculus is offered only in the final spring after its gateway prerequisite is feasible; it therefore follows optimisation, rather than being claimed as an earlier foundation. Introductory economics supports Public Economics before the later specialised microeconomics course. All formal prerequisites and term offerings are checked separately.

alternatives.label: Econometrics, data science & predictive modelling
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum retains the econometric and economic core but adds software development, neural networks, AI ethics and AI/business applications, making data science and predictive modelling a visible organising strand rather than calling the whole programme simply Econometrics.
alternatives.concept: Mathematics, statistics and econometrics are combined with programming, software, databases, machine learning and neural networks, emphasising how data are organised and used to build predictive models.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest-match curriculum, this route replaces accounting/corporate finance, public economics, numerical methods and general ethics with database management, software development, neural networks, AI ethics and explicit AI/business applications. Those changes make computational data science and predictive modelling, rather than the broad economics-and-operations-research core, the additional organising logic.
progression: Programming, data handling and economics start in Semester 1. Mathematical Methods and Research Methods & Statistics precede linear algebra, probability and machine learning. Algorithms & Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms, and machine learning precedes neural networks. Multivariate statistics is placed before Econometrics. Logic is later than advanced algorithms, but the introductory programming course already supplies elementary logic/sets and the formal prerequisite; no extra prerequisite is invented.

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics & financial decisions
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum has a large mathematical/statistical and economic core, with accounting and practical financial decisions as a defined application strand. The label does not present its limited finance-specific content as the specialist Quantitative Finance major.
alternatives.concept: Mathematical and statistical modelling are combined with empirical economics, financial-statement analysis, practical investment and budgeting decisions, and behavioural and business study.
alternatives.distinctness: The retained quantitative core is reorganised around practical economic/business and financial decisions. Relative to the first option, venture planning, relational data management, practical finance and behavioural economics replace advanced algorithms, logic/discrete mathematics, AI optimisation and reinforcement learning. These are specific operating/data/decision contributions, not four arbitrary substitutions or four specialist-finance courses. Accounting and finance together comprise 15 EC; the broader business/behavioural contributions are explicitly complementary.
progression: Venture/business planning precedes Money, Banking & Finance, satisfying its formal prerequisite and providing specific business-model/market-validation knowledge. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, probability, numerical methods and Advanced Calculus. Research Methods & Statistics and multivariate statistics precede Econometrics. Introductory programming precedes algorithms and AI decision-making. The broad introduction to economics precedes Public Economics, followed by the specialised microeconomic and behavioural courses. All formal prerequisites and offerings are checked separately.

candidates.label: Analytics and Operations Research in Logistics

routeSelection.basis: Econometrics is retained as the broad continuation of the common econometric field and is first in the current 2026–2027 official major table. No route was selected for UCR fit. Within it, the first listed eligible optional course (Quantitative Methods for Data Science) and seminar (Forecasting) instantiate the otherwise generic 20-EC major; Advanced Econometrics is compulsory. The retained minor12/electives12 branch is valid; minor15/electives9 is also permitted.

selection.assessment: Three evidenced educational choices survive the course-content and programme-level review: quantitative economics/optimisation, computational data science, and applied quantitative economics with financial decisions. The last is a qualified business/financial application of substantial quantitative economics, not a reproduction of the Quantitative Finance major. Logistics was tested and rejected because optimisation/algorithms alone do not provide the defining logistics/supply-chain content needed for a distinct complete programme. No official-major-order claim governs the ordering of UCR alternatives. Every generator row retains one core/candidate owner; maximum reached only after these three pass substantive and feasibility checks.

blocks: Both study elementary differential and integral calculus; UCR also introduces complex numbers and differential equations. This is a partial subject relationship, not equivalent coverage of the full analysis sequence.
UCR Advanced Calculus explicitly extends calculus to multiple dimensions. This is a meaningful multivariable-calculus relationship; it does not recreate every dedicated vector-calculus topic.
Both provide foundational statistical methods; UCR Research Methods & Statistics is broader and more applied than the comparator's dedicated introductory statistics course.
Both cover multivariate statistical analysis; UCR teaches it in a behavioural-science research context rather than an econometrics-specific context.

The external programme has a further separate Analysis course. UCR’s introductory and advanced calculus courses are already shown against the most directly identified introductory and multivariable components; no extra course is invented.
Kept separate: matching the identical title alone did not establish equivalent content for this additional external methods component.
Both teach introductory programming. UCR’s enriched outline specifies Python; the current formal external schedule does not establish its programming language, so no Java comparison is asserted.

The actual UCR optimisation outline includes continuous/global search and project work in convex optimisation and linear/nonlinear programming. This identifies direct optimisation content, while its broader AI-search emphasis differs from a dedicated nonlinear-optimisation course.

UCR Advanced Algorithms explicitly studies algorithmic solution methods for optimisation problems and advanced optimisation projects. This is an algorithmic-method relationship; no unverified dedicated integer-programming or combinatorial syllabus is claimed.

UCR Software Development develops C++/Haskell programming, testing and implementation beyond the introductory gateway. It supplies a direct advanced-programming relationship in the data-science option, without claiming the same external language or syllabus.

UCR Microeconomics & Behavior supplies the stronger dedicated microeconomic counterpart: consumer decisions, market structure, strategic behaviour and equilibrium. Its behavioural emphasis and scope differ from the external course.
Both develop regression-based econometric estimation and empirical analysis; the comparator continues with additional econometrics courses beyond UCR's single dedicated course.

UCR studies practical financial-data, risk, investment and budgeting decisions. This is a limited financial-decision relationship, not a claim of equivalent mathematical finance, broad banking coverage or the Quantitative Finance major.
Both provide structured ethical reasoning, but UCR Ethics is general rather than specifically focused on econometrics.
Career preparation is kept distinct from UCR’s general personal/academic-development requirement.
This separate 1-EC career unit is not folded into PPD.
The dedicated advanced econometrics course has no additional scheduled UCR equivalent beyond the single Econometrics course already shown.
The formal major course is retained separately; no exact course-specific syllabus was established from the script-only catalogue.
The compulsory 12-EC forecasting seminar is not replaced by general machine learning or the optional independent-research element.

notes.text: These UCR programmes provide substantial mathematical, statistical, computational and economic study, with one dedicated Econometrics course. Erasmus continues through additional econometrics, time series, mathematical economics, a 20-EC major and a required 10-EC thesis. UCR’s finance strand is practical financial decision-making and accounting, not the specialist Quantitative Finance major. Optional independent research adds 15 EC outside the scheduled 180 EC and is not a guaranteed replacement for Erasmus’s thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: The English-taught International Bachelor Econometrics and Operations Research at Erasmus School of Economics combines mathematics, statistics, programming and algorithms with economic and business problems. Students develop econometric and optimisation models, choose a major and complete an individual thesis. This comparison shows the 2026–2027 curriculum with the Econometrics major and a 12-EC minor.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options offer substantial quantitative study with different priorities: economics and optimisation, computational data science, or economic and financial decisions. They combine mathematical/statistical foundations with econometrics and programming, while differing from Erasmus’s longer specialist sequence and required major seminar and thesis. The financial option uses practical finance and accounting; it does not reproduce the Quantitative Finance major. Shared rows indicate meaningful partial relationships; blank cells preserve other content and gaps.

curriculum.limitation: This is one permitted route in the 2026–2027 curriculum. The minor and School elective subjects remain open within approved choices. A15-EC minor leaves 9 EC of electives. The public overview describes a redesigned 2027–2028 curriculum, so check the rules for your year.
